Dothan
DOH-thuhn
proper noun (place)
Hebrew Dothan; a town north of Shechem, the place where Joseph was sold and where Elisha was surrounded by horses and chariots of fire.

See also: Dothan

📖 Biblical Definition

Dothan was a town in the hill country north of Shechem, the setting of two memorable scenes of God's hidden providence. There Joseph, sent by his father to seek his brothers, found them at Dothan, and there they stripped him, cast him into a pit, and sold him to the Ishmaelites bound for Egypt (Gen 37:17-28) — the cruel act by which God, unseen, began to send a deliverer ahead of His people. Centuries later, Dothan was the home of the prophet Elisha when the king of Syria, learning that the prophet revealed his war-plans to Israel, sent a great host by night to seize him; "and they came by night, and compassed the city about" (2 Kgs 6:14). Elisha's servant rose to see the city surrounded and cried out in fear; but Elisha prayed, "LORD, I pray thee, open his eyes, that he may see. And the LORD opened the eyes of the young man; and he saw: and, behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha" (2 Kgs 6:17). Dothan stands in the dictionary as the place of unseen providence and unseen armies, a witness that God works His saving purpose through the malice of men, and that His people are guarded by hosts the natural eye cannot see, so that "they that be with us are more than they that be with them."

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A town north of Shechem where Joseph was sold by his brothers (Gen 37:17) and where Elisha, surrounded by the Syrian host, prayed and his servant saw the mountain full of horses and chariots of fire (2 Kgs 6:13-17).

DOTHAN, proper noun. A town in the hill country north of Shechem.

Where Joseph found his brothers and was sold to the Ishmaelites (Gen 37:17-28).

The home of Elisha, surrounded by a Syrian host sent to seize him (2 Kgs 6:13-14).

Where Elisha prayed and his servant's eyes were opened.

Where the mountain was seen full of horses and chariots of fire (2 Kgs 6:17).

📖 Key Scripture

Gen 37:17 — "And the man said, They are departed hence; for I heard them say, Let us go to Dothan. And Joseph went after his brethren, and found them in Dothan."

2 Kgs 6:16 — "And he answered, Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them."

2 Kgs 6:17 — "And Elisha prayed, and said, LORD, I pray thee, open his eyes, that he may see. And the LORD opened the eyes of the young man; and he saw: and, behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha."

Psa 34:7 — "The angel of the LORD encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Dothan needs no defense from redefinition; its lessons are the hidden providence that works good through men's malice, and the unseen armies of God that guard His people.

expand to see more

Providence-blind correction. To the natural eye, Joseph's sale at Dothan was sheer cruelty and loss; in truth God was sending a savior ahead to preserve life, as Joseph later confessed, "ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good" (Gen 50:20). The dictionary holds that God works His saving purposes even through the sins of men, overruling malice for mercy; the believer, like Joseph, may not see the design in the pit, but the hand of God is at work in the darkest providence.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the reality of the unseen armies of God. Elisha's servant saw only the surrounding enemy until God opened his eyes to the mountain full of fiery horses and chariots. The dictionary commends this faith: the people of God are guarded by hosts the natural eye cannot see, "the angel of the LORD encampeth round about them that fear him" (Psa 34:7), and they that be with us are more than they that be with them, however the visible odds may appear.
